comments.author: @giannisolga5191
comments.text: I thought I had no connections to Uganda. But as the video proceeded, things kept popping into my head. Having swum at the very site in Gombe Tanzania where Burton and Speke had stopped, where they established that Lake Tanganyika had no outlet to the north and therefore was not the source of the Nile, my imagination went wild. Then standing at Skeke Gulf near Mwanza I had the same joy looking out onto Lake Victoria and imagining the thrill Speke must have had. I wasn’t aware that he circumambulated the lake and found the outlet in the north. Logical, but I didn’t know it and hadn’t thought of it. Thank you for that information. When I worked in Rhodesia my mentor asked me: what is the commonest tumor in African children? My guesses were all wrong. The answer: Burkitt’s lymphoma. This was established by Dennis Burkitt working at the University of Kampala and reignited research worldwide into the viral cause of cancer. Third connection is that I went to the source of the Mississippi in northern Minnesota and established just what you said with the Nile. Working my way upstream I was standing on rocks and from all directions flowed tiny rivulets. To say this or that rivulet was it seemed almost moot. Fourth connection (whew, we’re getting close) is when I worked in Saudia Arabia once motoring near Jeddah we passed an open truck carrying about 20 African women in bright robes crowded together laughing and singing. I was told they were part of Idi Amin’s harem he’d brought with him in exile. Last connection: Zohran Mamdani, mayor of New York City, was born in Kampala and lived there until he was seven years old. Thank you for this wonderful video.

replies.author: @WhereonEarth4K
replies.text: Five connections in one comment might be a record - thank you for all of it, especially the Burkitt's lymphoma thread, that's a piece of medical history tied to Kampala that deserves far more recognition than it gets. And the Mississippi comparison captures exactly what we were going for with the Nile's own tangle of "sources."
